name: aux-sticky
description: CANDIDATE, NEVER FLASHED, NOT BEING PURSUED. Stops the unit releasing AUX when the saved AUX input setting (Auxiliary_Status) goes to zero, so once AUX has been activated it stays selected until the user changes source. It follows the setting, not the AUX signal, so on its own it does not address intermittent audio on the AUX input (see docs/AUX_SIGNAL.md; aux-signal-switch pairs with it for that). Two edits: the +0x10c edit is aux-autoswitch's inert GetMediaDevice nop (that branch is never taken, because the AUX media device is registered unconditionally), kept so this set is a superset of aux-autoswitch; the +0x118 edit retargets the release branch to the shared return path, keeping its condition. Control flow verified under emulation on all three images (NAV, AUDIO_BT, AUDIO_BT_256): activates when the setting query turns non-zero, does not release when it returns to zero.
summary: removes the bail-out **and** turns "AUX setting switched off" into a no-op

status.label: Never flashed

patches.why: HandleAudioAuxInputStatusChnged +0x10c: remove the GetMediaDevice bail-out so ActivateSource() is reachable

handler +0x118: when the AUX input setting is zero, branch to the shared return path instead of the release branch, so an activated AUX stays selected. The condition is KEPT and only the target changes: the original is `beq cr7,+0x58` (the release path) and this is `beq cr7,+0x140` (the return path at handler+0x258). Writing `b +0x140` here instead makes the branch unconditional, so the activate path below it becomes unreachable and the handler can never select AUX at all.
